name: Infant-type Hemispheric Glioma ROS1-altered
aliases: Infantile High-grade Glioma with ROS1 Fusion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Molecular and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Infant-type Hemispheric Glioma

criteria.description: Histological evidence of high-grade glioma with infantile features
Detection of ROS1 gene rearrangement or fusion by molecular genetic testing
Clinical presentation in infancy or early childhood (typically under 2 years)
Neuroimaging showing a large hemispheric mass with features suggestive of high-grade glioma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of high-grade glioma plus molecular evidence of ROS1 fusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for ROS1 fusion is essential to distinguish from other infantile gliomas.

searchTerms: rapid onset of focal nerve problems
fast progression of localized brain deficits

pathognomonic.symptomName: Seizures refractory to standard antiepileptic drugs

common.symptomName: Macrocephaly due to intracranial mass effect
searchTerms: head enlargement due to mass effect

common.symptomName: Vomiting secondary to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: throwing up due to increased intracranial pressure
weakness on one side of body

occasional.symptomName: Headache in infants (manifested as inconsolable crying)
searchTerms: persistent crying due to head pain

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-diagnostic but may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI showing large, heterogeneously enhancing hemispheric mass with necrosis and edema
Mass effect with midline shift common
genetic: Presence of ROS1 gene fusion/rearrangement confirmed by FISH, RT-PCR, or NGS
Absence of other common infantile glioma fusions such as ALK, NTRK
other: Histopathology showing high-grade glioma features with infantile morphology
Immunohistochemistry positive for glial markers (GFAP) and ROS1 protein overexpression

distinguishingFeatures: NTRK1 gene fusion instead of ROS1
Similar clinical presentation but different molecular target

redFlags: Seizures refractory to multiple antiepileptic drugs
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting and bulging fontanelle
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Parker M et al. Infant-type hemispheric glioma with ROS1 fusion: clinical and molecular characterization. Neuro Oncol. 2022;24(3):456-466.
